# Midas

> Midas is a free, open-source (MIT) AI meeting copilot for macOS. It captures the Mac's system audio, transcribes Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams or any other call on device with Whisper large-v3-turbo (MLX, Apple Silicon), and, when the user presses Answer, Claude Code drafts a reply over MCP and shows it in a floating panel that is hidden from screen sharing. No bot joins the call and audio never leaves the Mac.

Key facts:

- Platform: Apple Silicon Mac, macOS 14.4 or later. Not available for Intel Macs, Windows or Linux.
- Install: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/onurkagan/midas-meeting-copilot/main/install.sh | bash` sets up Xcode tools, Python and Claude Code if missing, builds Midas and installs Midas.app. Running it again updates Midas.
- Audio capture: Core Audio process tap; no meeting bot, no virtual audio driver. Only system audio, not the microphone.
- Transcription: local Whisper large-v3-turbo via mlx-whisper; Turkish and English by default, configurable.
- AI: Claude through Claude Code, connected with an MCP server (tools: wait_for_conversation, show_answer, get_transcript, midas_status). Model (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) and effort are chosen in the panel.
- Privacy: audio is processed in memory and not saved; text goes to Claude only when the user presses Answer or Summary. Transcripts are saved locally as Markdown.
- Panel: NSWindow.sharingType = .none, no Dock icon, never takes focus; hotkeys ⌃⌥A (Answer), ⌃⌥M (show/hide), ⌃⌥P (pause).
- Usage: about 4k tokens of context per answer; a 30-minute meeting on Opus uses roughly 0.1% of a Claude Max plan's 5-hour limit (author's measurement).
